MACAT usage guide

MACAT, the MERFISH Allen CCF Alignment Tool, aligns MERFISH mouse-brain sections to the Allen Mouse Brain Common Coordinate Framework and labels every cell with its Allen region. This guide takes you from installation to a finished, downloaded alignment. Written for v0.7.0; the screenshots are from that version.

Overview

MACAT runs as a local web app: a small server on your computer and a page in your browser. Each alignment is a job that moves through six steps, and is saved as it goes, so you can stop at any point and resume later.

MACAT works through the six steps in this order:

1Input2Orientation3Reference level 4Registration5Curation6Results
  1. Input: point MACAT at a section (a local folder or an s3:// path) and create a job.
  2. Orientation: choose coronal or sagittal, whole or half section, and rotate or flip it upright.
  3. Reference level: pick the Allen atlas slice that matches the section.
  4. Registration: MACAT aligns the atlas to the section automatically, in seconds.
  5. Curation: check the fit by eye and refine it, globally and, if needed, locally.
  6. Results: review every cell's Allen region, the figures and QC, and download them.

It supports coronal and sagittal sections, whole sections and coronal hemisections, and experiments in a local folder or on Amazon S3. It does not align other species or 3D volumes, and it does not prove that an alignment is anatomically correct: the QC supports a fit, it does not certify it.

To run MACAT you need: Python 3.11, about 2 GB of disk for MACAT and its packages, plus about 600 MB for the Allen atlas (downloaded on first use), and 8 GB of RAM. No GPU and no Node.js. MACAT is tested on Linux, Windows and macOS (Apple Silicon).

Once, to build the Allen reference files (below), you also need: a 9.2 GB download, about 17 GB of free disk while it runs, and 22 GB of RAM. The finished files take under 10 MB, and the download can be deleted afterwards.

Install

Get the code:

git clone https://github.com/Vizgen/MACAT.git
cd MACAT

Then create the Python environment with one of these three options. Run every later command from this folder, with the environment active.

Option A: uv (quickest)

Install uv first; it installs Python 3.11 for you if you don't have it.

uv venv --python 3.11
source .venv/bin/activate          # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
uv pip install -r requirements-web.txt

Option B: conda

conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate macat
Windows, first time with conda

Install Miniconda, open Anaconda Prompt and run conda init cmd.exe once. From then on, any new Command Prompt window can use conda.

Option C: plain pip (Python 3.11 already installed)

python3.11 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate          # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements-web.txt

Build the Allen reference files (once)

MACAT compares your sections with tables derived from the Allen Brain Cell Atlas. Their licence (CC BY-NC 4.0) permits noncommercial use only, so they are not shipped with MACAT: you build them once from Allen's public release. The build downloads about 9.2 GB, needs about 17 GB of free disk and 22 GB of RAM while it runs, and takes about 15 minutes. It uses its own, separate environment.

# conda
conda env create -f environment_allen_reference.yml
conda activate allen_reference

# ...or uv (or pip, with Python 3.10 installed)
uv venv --python 3.10 .venv-allen-reference
source .venv-allen-reference/bin/activate   # Windows: .venv-allen-reference\Scripts\activate
uv pip install -r requirements-allen-reference.txt

# then build
python scripts/data/fetch_allen_sources.py
python scripts/data/fetch_abc_reference.py
python scripts/data/fetch_abc_section_reference.py

Switch back to MACAT's environment afterwards. Until the files are built, MACAT warns at startup, and registration stops with a message naming the missing file. Checksums to confirm a build are in data/reference/README.md.

Start MACAT

From the MACAT folder, with its environment active:

python -m uvicorn web.server:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8700

Wait for the line Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8700 (Press CTRL+C to quit), then open http://127.0.0.1:8700 in Chrome, Firefox, Edge or Safari. The first registration also downloads the Allen atlas (about 600 MB) to ~/.brainglobe.

"Address already in use"

On Windows this reads [Errno 10048] ... only one usage of each socket address. Something already holds port 8700: often a MACAT server you started earlier, or VS Code forwarding a port. Open http://127.0.0.1:8700 to check, or start on another port, such as --port 18700, and open http://127.0.0.1:18700 instead.

Prepare your data

Keep your experiments the way MERSCOPE writes them, all under one data folder, on your computer or as an s3:// prefix:

your_data_folder/
├── experiment_A/
│   ├── region_R1/
│   │   ├── cell_metadata.csv
│   │   ├── cell_by_gene.csv
│   │   └── images/
│   │       ├── mosaic_DAPI_z3.tif
│   │       └── micron_to_mosaic_pixel_transform.csv
│   └── region_R2/ ...
└── experiment_B/ ...
FileNeededUsed for
cell_metadata.csvRequiredcell positions (EntityID, center_x, center_y, in µm)
cell_by_gene.csvRequiredexpression QC and the marker-gene background
images/mosaic_DAPI_z3.tif + images/micron_to_mosaic_pixel_transform.csvOptionalthe DAPI background; without them, cell density is shown
detected_transcripts.parquet (or .csv)Optionalthe transcript-density background

MACAT reads files by these exact names. If a download adds a suffix, such as cell_metadata_S1R1.csv, rename it to cell_metadata.csv, and likewise for the others.

No data yet? Try an example

  • Vizgen's MERFISH mouse-brain showcase, from the Vizgen website. Put each slice in your data folder as <experiment>/region_*/, keeping its images/ folder inside.
  • Allen annotated data: 12 published sections (whole coronal, coronal hemisection and sagittal) whose correct orientation, level and per-cell regions are known, so you can check MACAT's answers. Download links and build commands are in docs/allen_annotated_data.md; set your data folder to the sections folder it builds.

To read experiments from S3, install the AWS CLI and give it credentials that can read your bucket (aws configure or AWS_PROFILE).

1Input: create a job

The first page sets your data folder, creates new jobs and lists the jobs you already have.

  1. Set the data folder. Press Set… (or Change), paste the folder path or s3:// prefix, and press Save. MACAT scans it and remembers it. It scans again only when you press Rescan, so press that after adding experiments.
  2. Pick a section from Your sections. Every region_* folder in the data folder is listed, grouped by experiment. Sections with known answers show their atlas level, for example region_R1 · level 286 ±9.
  3. Or paste one region folder into …or experiment folder: a local path or s3://<bucket>/<experiment>/region_R1/.
  4. Name the job (optional). Letters, numbers, spaces, - and _ only. The name titles the job and every file you download from it. Leave it as it is to use the folder name.
  5. Press Create job.
Good to know

The data folder can only be set on the computer MACAT runs on (or through an SSH tunnel to it). A path pasted into Experiment folder is read where it is; nothing is copied, except files fetched from S3.

2Orientation: set the section upright

Match your tissue to the way the atlas is cut.

  1. Section plane: Coronal or Sagittal.
  2. Section (coronal only): Whole, or Left half / Right half for a hemisection.
  3. Rotation and Flip: turn the tissue until the dorsal side is up. For a sagittal section, also put anterior on the left.
  4. Press Confirm orientation.
Changing an earlier step

Going back and confirming a different orientation or level discards the registration and curation that followed it.

3Reference level: pick the matching atlas slice

  1. Move the Atlas AP index slider (ML index for sagittal sections), or use − / +, until the landmarks match: hippocampus in red, ventricles in cyan. The first load of the atlas takes about 30 seconds.
  2. Press Run registration.

For a section with a known answer, such as the Allen annotated data, the page says where its published registration puts it, and the slider starts there.

4Registration: automatic alignment

MACAT fits the 3D atlas to the tissue at the level you chose, reads an Allen region for every cell, and moves on to curation by itself. It takes a few seconds.

The summary shows how many cells landed in an annotated Allen region. That is coverage, not accuracy: the rest fell off the section edge or on unannotated tissue. Region boundaries are corrected by hand in step 5.

If you come back to this step later, press Continue to curation.

5Curation: refine the alignment

Step 5 shows the atlas outlines over your tissue. You can accept the automatic fit as it is, or refine it in two ways: Global affine moves, scales and rotates the whole atlas; Local correction bends it in places. Fit globally first, then correct locally.

Panel controls

ControlWhat it does
AlignmentAuto shows the automatic fit (read-only); Manual is where you edit.
Edit modeGlobal affine or Local correction, described below.
Undo · Reset local · Reset allUndo the last edit; drop the local correction only; or go back to the automatic fit.
Alignment regionsWhich outlines to align against: Landmarks (a few high-contrast structures) or Allen hierarchy Depth 2–4, coarse to fine. Click a region pill to clear its fill; its outline stays.
Overlay displayOutline thickness and fill opacity. Display only.
BackgroundDAPI (or cell density, without DAPI) or Marker genes: canonical markers coloured like the Allen division they mark, so each division and its outline should coincide. Click a gene pill to toggle it.
Transform · Local correctionRead-outs of the current fit: shift, rotation and scale; nodes moved, the largest move, and min |J| (see Results).

Global affine

  • Drag inside the box to move the atlas.
  • Edge handles scale one axis: use the top and bottom handles to fix a vertical squash.
  • Corner handles scale both axes.
  • The knob above the box rotates.

In every mode, the mouse wheel zooms and dragging empty space pans. In Local correction, the tool gets the press first, so hold Shift to pan over the tissue.

Local correction

Local correction bends the atlas with a warp grid: a lattice of nodes over the section. Moving a node pulls the atlas around it smoothly. Two tools move them:

  • Direct drag: grab a white or blue atlas boundary and pull it onto the matching DAPI edge. If a drag is unavailable, click the line once and then click its target. Work from large landmarks to small ones, and use Undo if a pull doesn't help.
  • Advanced grid: drag the grid nodes themselves. Corner nodes stay pinned, and edge nodes slide only along their own edge.

Warp layers: going further than one grid allows

Each node can move only so far; the limit is shown under Grid density. A move past it is refused with "displacement exceeds limit". When that happens, press Add layer: the current grid is baked into a layer and a fresh grid is laid over the corrected section, so you can keep correcting from where you are.

  • Up to 8 layers in all, counting the live grid.
  • Remove last discards the most recently baked layer.
  • Undo stops at a layer boundary: use Remove last to go back further.

Grid density: reach vs local detail

GridNode reachUse it for
13×13 (default)1×the most local control: small, precise corrections
9×91.5×moderate corrections
5×53×the widest reach: large, smooth corrections

The exact limit in µm for your section is shown under the buttons.

Add a layer before switching density

Switching density discards the live grid's correction; it is not saved as a layer. To keep it, press Add layer first, then switch. Layers already baked are kept.

Confirm

When the outlines sit where you want them, press Confirm alignment at the bottom of the panel. You can confirm the automatic fit unchanged. Finalizing takes about a minute, then Results opens. Leaving step 5 with unconfirmed edits asks you first, because Results would otherwise show the previous result.

6Results: review and download

Results shows the final per-cell labels, figures, statistics and QC, and the downloads.

Download full report (.zip) collects everything: per-cell labels, region tables, GeoJSON polygons, every figure panel from both the automatic and curated runs, the hex-bin QC, and a manifest.json recording the MACAT version and atlas.

Alignment recordMeaning
Cells labelledcells inside an annotated Allen region: coverage, not accuracy
vs automaticthe same figure before curation; a drop is worth checking
Atlas sliceAP index (coronal) or ML index (sagittal)
Global transformshift, rotation and scale from curation
Local warpnodes moved, largest move, and min |J|, which must stay well above 0, or the warp would fold tissue

Compare with automatic alignment shows the figures before curation.

Figures

Statistics and QC

All tables sort by clicking a column header.

CheckWhat it tells youKeep in mind
Region compositioncells per Allen region, as a share of mapped cellsdownload it as CSV
Whole-section correlation (r)one point per gene shared with the Allen panel: its mean counts in the Allen section at your level against this sectiona tissue-level check of the level choice; curation cannot change it
Region specificitywhether each region (≥ 50 cells) matches its own Allen profile better than any other region's. PASS when the median self-correlation is at least 0.30a highlighted best match means a region resembles another more than itself; a neighbour or fibre tract is usually harmless, a distant match is worth checking
Per-region agreementwhether each region resembles its own reference at alluse it to find the few bad regions in an otherwise sound fit
Spatial hex-bin QCa map of where expression agrees less with the mapped region, in 100 µm hexagonsexploratory, not PASS/FAIL; compare runs only at the same bin size

The QC thresholds are provisional, and the QC supports a fit rather than certifying it. Judge the numbers together with the overlay. Full details, including the per-cell table's columns, are in docs/interpreting_results.md.

Job deliverables

In report.zipContent
per_cell/every cell with its Allen region, curated and automatic
geometry_curated/Allen region polygons in the section's own coordinates (GeoJSON)
figures_curated/, figures_auto/regions over the background; cells coloured by region
region_tables_*/per-region cell counts, region × gene counts, per-region QC
hex_bin_qc_*/the spatial QC map and its per-bin table
merscope_vizualizer_*/cell → Allen region, ready to import into the MERSCOPE Vizualizer

Press New job at the bottom of the panel to start another alignment.

Manage jobs

Every job you create is listed under Resume a job on the step 1 page.

  • Resume: click a row to open that job where you left it. You can move back to earlier steps from the left rail.
  • Sort: click a column header.
  • One job: the ⬇ button in its row downloads its report (completed jobs only); the red button deletes it.
  • Select several with the check boxes, then Download .zip (completed jobs only; others are skipped, and the page says which) or Delete.
  • Notes: click add a note to label a job.

Jobs are stored in the MACAT folder under pipeline_output/jobs/<job ID>/, one folder per job. To keep them elsewhere, set ALLEN_OUT_ROOT before starting MACAT. Deleting a job removes its folder.

Stop and restart

  1. Close the browser tab.
  2. In the terminal running the server, press Ctrl+C. Wait for Finished server process.

To start again later, open a new terminal, go to the MACAT folder, activate the environment and start the server:

cd path/to/MACAT
conda activate macat               # or: source .venv/bin/activate
python -m uvicorn web.server:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8700

Your jobs, notes and data folder are all kept, and you can create a new job straight away.

Open results in the MERSCOPE Vizualizer

The report includes a cell → Allen region table for the Vizualizer: merscope_vizualizer_curated/TO_MERSCOPE_VIZUALIZER_allen_regions_<job name>_curated.csv.

  1. In the Vizualizer, open the assembled experiment for the same region.
  2. Choose File › Import Data › Metadata › Cells.
  3. Set Data format to CSV, tick Categories file and select the TO_MERSCOPE_VIZUALIZER_allen_regions_…_curated.csv file.
  4. Tick the fields to import, such as allen_acronym or the ontology levels, and press Import.
  5. Colour the cells by an imported field to explore the regions.

Troubleshooting

SymptomFix
address already in use / Errno 10048The port is taken. Check http://127.0.0.1:8700, or start with --port 18700.
ModuleNotFoundErrorThe environment isn't active. Activate it and start again.
Could not import module "web.server"Start from the MACAT folder.
Startup warning, or registration stops, about a missing Allen reference fileBuild the Allen reference files.
The page looks old after an updateHard-reload: Ctrl+Shift+R (Cmd+Shift+R on macOS).
A section is missing from Your sectionsCheck it is <data folder>/<experiment>/region_*/ with both cell tables, then press Rescan.
Saving is slow or fails on Windows, in a OneDrive folderKeep outputs out of OneDrive: set ALLEN_OUT_ROOT=C:\MACAT_output before starting.
A local move is refused: "displacement exceeds limit"Press Add layer and continue, or choose a coarser grid density (add a layer first).

More, including S3 errors and remote machines, in docs/troubleshooting.md.
